messages:
Acme Support: Hi team — since last night's deploy (~02:12 UTC) our knowledge-check endpoint started returning made-up compliance citations and future dates. Example response (redacted):
```json
{"answer":"Per SEC Reg. 45B, Acme is required to...","source":"https://sec.gov/regulations/45b","date":"2028-04-01"}
```
The link is bogus and the date is in the future. Request id: req_9a7f3c. Model reported in headers: redwood-instruct-2.4-latopt. Can we get this investigated? We had no issues before 2024-11-02.

Maya: thanks for the report — can you paste the prompt and the raw request (headers + body) and any other request ids? Also your org id.

Acme Support: prompt and sample payload attached:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_9a7f3c" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-instruct-2.4-latopt","prompt":"List regulatory citations relevant to Acme's widget business.","temperature":0.0}'
```
Org: acme-inc-42
We also have another id req_9a7f9 that returned a different made-up CEO quote.

Jordan: looking at routing logs — req_9a7f3c went to pool: dedicated-latopt-3 -> variant: quant-pt-8 (fp8-ish path). There's a config we rolled out at 02:00 UTC that changes fallback ordering to prefer the latency-optimized quant variant for short prompts. @vikram any known FP8 artifact patterns?

Vikram: FP8/quant kernels can induce confident wrong attributions when internal attention keys degrade on rare token combos; we've seen invented URLs and shifted dates. Need repro with seq len and temperature fixed. Can Acme run the same prompt with temp=0 and temp=0.3 and include the full JSON response with model headers? Also try model=redwood-instruct-2.4 (non-latopt).

Acme Support: ran tests, attached two responses: temp=0 -> fabricated link + 2028 date; temp=0.3 -> similar but different url. Using redwood-instruct-2.4 (non-latopt) returned accurate citations (matched our internal KB). So this is reproducible and tied to -latopt variant.

Maya: good repro — escalation opened. I'm tagging eng-runtime and ml. Priya moving to urgent CS handling and offering credit. @Sasha Bot please create incident with severity=high and include request ids. :rotating_light:

Sasha Bot: Incident INC-2034 created: 'latopt quant variant producing fabricated citations' — assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

Jordan: quick hypothesis: the quant variant's KV cache trimming interacts with causal prefix mismatch; when prefix is short the model hallucinates defaults. Short-term mitigation: route that org to stable (non-latopt) for 24h and disable the new fallback policy. I'll prepare a routing override. Need owner approval.

Priya: approved. Maya please confirm customer opt-in for rollback. I'll notify billing for a one-time credit.

Acme Support: confirmed they want immediate routing to stable variant and an explanation. They also asked for their logs to be retained for 90 days for audit.

Vikram: follow-ups: we'll run a micro-canary with synthetic prompts to reproduce rate, add regression test for citation hallucinations, and inspect fp8 kernel numerics. Expect initial findings in ~6 hours.

Jordan: routing override set: acme-inc-42 pinned to redwood-instruct-2.4 for now. Monitoring alert set for similar patterns across other orgs. I'll post PR with config rollback ref: rwd/infra#1129.

Maya: thanks everyone. Assigned actions summarized: (1) eng-runtime routing override (Jordan), (2) ML root-cause and tests (Vikram), (3) CS customer credit + retention (Priya), (4) incident docs + retention (Maya). I'll follow up in 6h. :white_check_mark:
